title: What If Every Oyster in the Ocean Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every oyster vanished? The first thing you'd notice isn't the menu. It's the water.
One oyster can filter up to fifty gallons of water a day, trapping sediment and pollution.
Within a season, bays would grow murkier, and less sunlight would reach the seagrass below.
Oyster reefs are habitat. Crabs, shrimp, snails and young fish all shelter in their crevices.
And the reefs break waves. A football-field-sized reef can save a community about eighty-five thousand dollars a year.
We've already lost about eighty-five percent of oyster reefs worldwide. Losing the rest would hit coasts hard.
